result.topic_en: A transformation formula, valid when αβ = π², for series of divisor functions σ_{-s}(n) multiplied by the integral φ_s(nα) = ∫_0^∞ x^{s-1} e^{-x²-a²/x²} dx, with its special cases s = 1 and s = 0.
result.transcription:
Add. Ms a 94^{18 (3)}
(3)
Formulae connected with the divisor problem, etc

If $\int_0^\infty x^{s-1} e^{-x^2 - \frac{a^2}{x^2}}\,dx = \phi_s(a)$
then
$\alpha^{\frac{1-s}{2}}\{\sigma_{-s}(1)\phi_s(\alpha) + \sigma_{-s}(2)\phi_s(2\alpha) + \sigma_{-s}(3)\phi_s(3\alpha) + \cdots\}$
$-\beta^{\frac{1-s}{2}}\{\sigma_{-s}(1)\phi_s(\beta) + \sigma_{-s}(2)\phi_s(2\beta) + \sigma_{-s}(3)\phi_s(3\beta) + \cdots\}$
$= \frac14\Gamma(\frac{s}{2})\zeta(s)\{\beta^{\frac{1-s}{2}} - \alpha^{\frac{1-s}{2}}\} + \frac14\Gamma(-\frac{s}{2})\zeta(-s)\{\beta^{\frac{1+s}{2}} - \alpha^{\frac{1+s}{2}}\}$,
provided that $\alpha\beta = \pi^2$, $\sigma_s(n)$ being the sum of the $s^{th}$ powers of the divisors of $n$.
If $s=1$, the above formula reduces to the known formula
$\{\sigma_{-1}(1)e^{-2\alpha} + \sigma_{-1}(2)e^{-4\alpha} + \sigma_{-1}(3)e^{-6\alpha} + \cdots\}$
$-\{\sigma_{-1}(1)e^{-2\beta} + \sigma_{-1}(2)e^{-4\beta} + \sigma_{-1}(3)e^{-6\beta} + \cdots\}$
$= \cdots\cdots$
with the condition $\alpha\beta = \pi^2$. If $s = 0$ we see that if
$\alpha\beta = \pi^2$, then
$\sqrt{\alpha}\{\frac14\gamma - \frac14\log 4\beta + d(1)\phi_0(\alpha) + d(2)\phi_0(2\alpha) + d(3)\phi_0(3\alpha) + \cdots\}$
$= \sqrt{\beta}\{\frac14\gamma - \frac14\log 4\alpha + d(1)\phi_0(\beta) + d(2)\phi_0(2\beta) + d(3)\phi_0(3\beta) + \cdots\}$.

methods.what: Definition of the integral φ_s(a), related to a modified Bessel function
Transformation formula under αβ = π² for the series Σ σ_{-s}(n) φ_s(nα), with constant terms involving Γ and ζ (a Voronoi/Koshliakov-type formula)
Special case s=1: transformation of the Lambert-type series Σ σ_{-1}(n) e^{-2nα} (related to the Dedekind eta function)
methods.quote: If $s=1$, the above formula reduces to the known formula

methods.what: Special case s=0: transformation for the divisor function d(n) series involving Euler's constant and log (Koshliakov's formula)
